where we used functoriality of \(\kappa\) (Step 2) to see that the map induced by \(\Theta\) on the Ext side is \(u\mapsto(\operatorname{pr}_j\circ\alpha\circ u)_j\). Put \(\alpha_j:=\operatorname{pr}_j\circ\alpha:K\to K_j\). For \(u\in\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal D}(\mathbb Q_\ell,K)\), the \(j\)-th component of the left-hand side applied to \(u\) is
\[
\alpha_j\circ\Psi_K(u)=\alpha_j\circ\varphi\circ F_X^*(u)\circ\psi^{-1}.
\]
By the hypothesis \(\alpha\circ\varphi=(\bigoplus_i\varphi_i)\circ F_X^*(\alpha)\), we have \(\alpha_j\circ\varphi=\operatorname{pr}_j\circ(\bigoplus_i\varphi_i)\circ F_X^*(\alpha)=\varphi_j\circ\operatorname{pr}'_j\circ F_X^*(\alpha)=\varphi_j\circ F_X^*(\alpha_j)\), the last equality being the compatibility of the additivity isomorphism with projections (Step 2). Hence the \(j\)-th component equals
\[
\varphi_j\circ F_X^*(\alpha_j)\circ F_X^*(u)\circ\psi^{-1}=\varphi_j\circ F_X^*(\alpha_j\circ u)\circ\psi^{-1}=\Psi_{K_j}(\alpha_j\circ u),
\]
which is precisely the \(j\)-th component of the right-hand side applied to \(u\). Since this holds for every \(j\) and every \(u\), \((\ast)\) is established.

**Step 5 (conclusion).** All the spaces in play are finite-dimensional over \(\mathbb Q_\ell\) and all the operators are automorphisms, by Step 1. Thus we may apply lemma_8 to \(V=H^0_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(X_k,K)\) with \(T_V=\Phi_K\), to \(W=\bigoplus_j H^0_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(X_k,K_j)\) with \(T_W=\bigoplus_j\Phi_{K_j}\), and to the intertwining isomorphism \(\Theta\) of Step 4: it yields
\[
\Phi_K\ \text{semisimple}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \bigoplus_{j=1}^m\Phi_{K_j}\ \text{semisimple}.
\]
By lemma_9 applied to the \(m\)-tuple \(V_j=H^0_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(X_k,K_j)\), \(T_j=\Phi_{K_j}\) (with \(m\ge1\), so the family is non-empty),
\[
\bigoplus_{j=1}^m\Phi_{K_j}\ \text{semisimple}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \Phi_{K_j}\ \text{is semisimple for every }j=1,\dots,m.
\]
Finally, lemma_5 states that for a finite-dimensional \(\mathbb Q_\ell\)-vector space \(V\) and an operator \(T\), \(T\) is semisimple on \(V\) if and only if its base change to \(\overline{\mathbb Q}_\ell\) is diagonalizable. Applying this to \((V,T)=(H^0_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(X_k,K),\Phi_K)\) and to each \((H^0_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(X_k,K_j),\Phi_{K_j})\), and chaining the equivalences, we obtain
\[
\Phi_K\ \text{diagonalizable over }\overline{\mathbb Q}_\ell\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \Phi_{K_j}\ \text{diagonalizable over }\overline{\mathbb Q}_\ell\ \text{for every }j,
\]
which is exactly the desired assertion. Both implications are contained in the chain of equivalences above. \(\blacksquare\)

lemma_367.statement: Let \(q=p^a\) be a prime power, let \(X\) be a smooth projective variety over \(\mathbb{F}_q\), let \(k=\overline{\mathbb{F}}_q\), and let \(\ell\neq p\) be prime. For \(n\ge0\), suppose the multiplication map \((H^1_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(X_k,\mathbb{Q}_\ell))^{\otimes n}\to H^n_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(X_k,\mathbb{Q}_\ell)\), \(\alpha_1\otimes\cdots\otimes\alpha_n\mapsto\alpha_1\cup\cdots\cup\alpha_n\), is surjective. If the \(q\)-power arithmetic Frobenius is semisimple on \(H^1_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(X_k,\mathbb{Q}_\ell)\), then it is semisimple on \(H^n_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(X_k,\mathbb{Q}_\ell)\).
lemma_367.proof:
Let V = H^1_et(X_k, Q_l). Since X is smooth projective over F_q, in particular proper, lemma_45_finite_frob applied to the constant sheaf Q_l on X_k with its natural arithmetic Frobenius structure shows that V is finite-dimensional over Q_l. For each r >= 0 let F_r denote the q-power arithmetic Frobenius automorphism on H^r_et(X_k, Q_l). By lemma_6a each F_r is a Q_l-linear automorphism. By lemma_5, semisimplicity over Q_l is equivalent to diagonalizability over Q_l_bar, so we may argue with semisimple Q_l-linear operators.

First prove a quotient fact. Let U be a finite-dimensional Q_l-vector space, let T in GL(U) be semisimple, and let W subset U be T-stable. If U/W = 0, the induced operator is semisimple trivially. Otherwise T(W) = W: indeed T(W) subset W by stability, and since T is invertible and U is finite-dimensional, dim T(W) = dim W, hence T(W) = W. Thus the induced operator T_bar on U/W lies in GL(U/W). By lemma_60, the minimal polynomial m_T of T is squarefree. Let pi:U -> U/W be the quotient map. For every u in U, m_T(T_bar)(pi(u)) = pi(m_T(T)u) = 0; since pi is surjective, m_T(T_bar) = 0. Hence the minimal polynomial m_{T_bar} divides m_T. A divisor of a squarefree polynomial is squarefree, so m_{T_bar} is squarefree. Applying lemma_60 again, T_bar is semisimple.

Now fix n. For n = 0, the multiplication map mu_0: Q_l -> H^0_et(X_k, Q_l) sends 1 to the unit class. With the usual convention that the empty cup product is the unit, lemma_cup_frob_equivariance gives F_0(1) = 1; hence mu_0 is equivariant for the identity operator on Q_l and for F_0. If H^0_et(X_k, Q_l) = 0, semisimplicity is trivial. Otherwise H^0_et(X_k, Q_l) is isomorphic to Q_l/ker(mu_0), and ker(mu_0) is stable under the identity operator. The quotient fact shows that the induced operator on Q_l/ker(mu_0) is semisimple. The induced map Q_l/ker(mu_0) -> H^0_et(X_k, Q_l) is an F-equivariant isomorphism, so lemma_8 gives semisimplicity of F_0.

Assume n >= 1. If V = 0, then V^{tensor n} = 0, and surjectivity of mu_n forces H^n_et(X_k, Q_l) = 0, which is semisimple. Assume V is nonzero. The cup product is Q_l-multilinear, so by the universal property of tensor products it defines a Q_l-linear map mu_n: V^{tensor n} -> H^n_et(X_k, Q_l), alpha_1 tensor ... tensor alpha_n maps to alpha_1 cup ... cup alpha_n. The hypothesis says mu_n is surjective.

By lemma_cup_frob_equivariance, for pure tensors we have mu_n(F_1^{tensor n}(alpha_1 tensor ... tensor alpha_n)) = (F_1 alpha_1) cup ... cup (F_1 alpha_n) = F_n(mu_n(alpha_1 tensor ... tensor alpha_n)). By linearity, mu_n intertwines F_1^{tensor n} and F_n.

Since F_1 is semisimple and invertible on the finite-dimensional space V, induction using lemma_35(i) shows that F_1^{tensor n} is semisimple on V^{tensor n}. Indeed, for n = 1 this is the hypothesis. If F_1^{tensor (n-1)} is semisimple, then F_1^{tensor n} = F_1^{tensor (n-1)} tensor F_1 is semisimple by lemma_35(i), because both factors are invertible semisimple operators on finite-dimensional spaces.

Let K = ker(mu_n). The intertwining relation implies that K is F_1^{tensor n}-stable: if v in K, then mu_n(F_1^{tensor n}v) = F_n(mu_n(v)) = 0. Applying the quotient fact to U = V^{tensor n}, T = F_1^{tensor n}, and W = K, the induced operator F_bar on V^{tensor n}/K is semisimple. If this quotient is zero, then H^n_et(X_k, Q_l) = 0 and we are done. Otherwise, the first isomorphism theorem gives a Q_l-linear isomorphism mu_bar: V^{tensor n}/K -> H^n_et(X_k, Q_l), mu_bar(v+K) = mu_n(v). The quotient is finite-dimensional because V^{tensor n} is finite-dimensional, so H^n_et(X_k, Q_l) is finite-dimensional. The intertwining relation says mu_bar(F_bar(v+K)) = F_n(mu_bar(v+K)). Since F_bar is invertible by the quotient fact and F_n is invertible by lemma_6a, lemma_8 implies that F_n is semisimple on H^n_et(X_k, Q_l). Finally, lemma_5 gives the equivalent diagonalizability over Q_l_bar.

This proves the desired statement for every n >= 0.

lemma_366.statement: Let \(q=p^a\) be a prime power, let \(X\) be a smooth projective geometrically connected variety over \(\mathbb{F}_q\) admitting an \(\mathbb{F}_q\)-rational point, let \(k=\overline{\mathbb{F}}_q\), and let \(\ell\neq p\) be prime. Then the \(q\)-power arithmetic Frobenius \((\mathrm{id}_{X_k}\times\operatorname{Spec}\sigma)^*\), \(\sigma(c)=c^q\), is semisimple on \(H^1_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(X_k,\mathbb{Q}_\ell)\).
lemma_366.proof:
Let x0 be an F_q-rational point of X, let k=overline(F_q), and let l!=p. Put V_X=H^1_et(X_k,Q_l). By the Albanese variety over the algebraically closed field k, there is an abelian variety B over k and an Albanese morphism beta:X_k->B with beta(x0)=0. Lemma_alb_h1_geometric applied to X_k over k with base point x0 gives an isomorphism of Q_l-vector spaces beta^*:H^1_et(B_k,Q_l)->V_X.

Since B, its group law, and beta are of finite type over k, and k is the union of the finite fields F_{q^r}, there exist an integer m>=1, an abelian variety B_m over F_{q^m}, and a morphism beta_m:X_{F_{q^m}}->B_m over F_{q^m} such that base change to k recovers B and beta. (Choose all defining equations and coefficients in one finite subfield; the group law descends as well.) The point x0 is still rational over F_{q^m}.

Let V_B=H^1_et(B_k,Q_l). By lemma_45_finite_frob applied to X_{F_{q^m}} over F_{q^m} and to B_m over F_{q^m}, V_X and V_B are finite-dimensional Q_l-vector spaces. By lemma_6a (applied over the base field F_{q^m}) the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius operators F_{q^m,X}=(id_{X_k} x Spec sigma_m)^* and F_{q^m,B_m}=(id_{B_k} x Spec sigma_m)^*, sigma_m(c)=c^{q^m}, are invertible Q_l-linear operators.

Because beta_m is defined over F_{q^m}, beta_m o F_{q^m,X}=F_{q^m,B_m} o beta_m as morphisms over F_{q^m}. Taking etale pullbacks and using contravariance yields beta^* o F_{q^m,B_m}=F_{q^m,X} o beta^*.

If B_m is the zero abelian variety, then V_B=0, and the isomorphism beta^* gives V_X=0; the zero operator is semisimple. Otherwise, lemma_h1_abelian_semisimple applied to B_m over F_{q^m} says that F_{q^m,B_m} is semisimple on V_B. Since beta^* is an isomorphism intertwining F_{q^m,B_m} with F_{q^m,X}, lemma_8 implies that F_{q^m,X} is semisimple on V_X.

Finally, lemma_150 states that for a smooth projective variety X over F_q, the q-power arithmetic Frobenius is semisimple on H^1_et(X_k,Q_l) if and only if the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius is semisimple there. Therefore the q-power arithmetic Frobenius (id_{X_k} x Spec sigma)^*, sigma(c)=c^q, is semisimple on H^1_et(X_k,Q_l).

lemma_projective_cohomology_vanishing.statement: Let \(k\) be an algebraically closed field, let \(\ell\) be a prime different from the characteristic of \(k\), and let \(Z\) be a projective scheme over \(k\) of Krull dimension at most \(r\), where \(r\ge 0\) is an integer. Then \(H^n_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(Z,\mathbb Q_\ell)=0\) for every integer \(n>2r\).
lemma_projective_cohomology_vanishing.proof:
Proof. Let d be the Krull dimension of Z, with d = -infinity if Z is empty. If Z is empty, the assertion is immediate.

Case 1: d = 0. Since Z is projective over k, it is quasi-compact and of finite type over k. Choose a finite affine open cover Z = U_1 union ... union U_t, with U_a = Spec A_a. Each U_a is a quasi-compact open subscheme of a finite type k-scheme, hence A_a is a finitely generated k-algebra. Since U_a is contained in Z, dim A_a = dim U_a <= dim Z = 0. A Noetherian ring of Krull dimension 0 is Artinian: its nilradical is nilpotent, and the quotient by the nilradical is a finite product of fields. Consequently Spec A_a is a finite discrete topological space. Thus each U_a is finite, and every point of U_a is open in U_a. Since U_a is open in Z, a subset open in U_a is open in Z, so every point of Z is open in Z. The underlying set of Z is the finite union of the finite sets U_a, so Z is a finite discrete scheme. A one-point scheme is affine, because any affine open containing its unique point is the whole scheme. A finite disjoint union of affine schemes is affine, since the coproduct of Spec A_1 and Spec A_2 is Spec(A_1 times A_2). Hence Z is affine. Applying lemma_ordinary_vanishing_affine_cover to X = Z, e = 0, m = 1, and U_1 = Z gives H^n_et(Z,Q_ell) = 0 for every n > 0. If n > 2r, then n > 0, so the desired vanishing follows in this case.

Case 2: d >= 1. Then r >= 1. Choose a closed immersion i : Z -> P^N_k. Since Z has positive dimension, N >= 1. Let L = i^*O_{P^N}(1). The line bundle O_{P^N}(1) is ample, and the pullback of an ample line bundle by a closed immersion is ample; hence L is ample on Z.

We first prove a hyperplane avoidance claim. Let W be a nonempty closed subscheme of P^N, and let C_1,...,C_t be the irreducible components of W_red; these are finite in number because P^N is noetherian. There exists a hyperplane H contained in P^N that contains none of the C_a. Indeed, let V = H^0(P^N,O(1)). Hyperplanes in P^N are parameterized by the dual projective space P(V^∨). For each a, let K_a be the vector subspace of V consisting of linear forms whose zero locus contains C_a. The set of hyperplanes containing C_a is P(K_a), a projective linear subspace of P(V^∨), hence closed. If C_a = P^N, then K_a = 0 and P(K_a) is empty. If C_a is a proper nonempty closed subset, then K_a is not all of V: if every linear form vanished on C_a, then C_a would be contained in every hyperplane, but the intersection of all hyperplanes is empty, since for any point one can choose a coordinate hyperplane not containing it. Thus each P(K_a) is a proper closed subset of P(V^∨). The dual projective space P(V^∨) is irreducible: it has a dense affine chart Spec k[y_1,...,y_N], whose coordinate ring is a domain. A finite union of proper closed subsets cannot cover an irreducible topological space: if X = F_1 union ... union F_t with all F_i closed and X irreducible, then X = F_a for some a. Hence there is a hyperplane avoiding all C_a. This proves the claim.

Now construct hyperplanes H_0,...,H_r inductively. Let W_0 = Z as a closed subscheme of P^N. For j = 0,...,r, if W_j is empty, choose any hyperplane H_j, which is possible because N >= 1, and set W_{j+1} to be the empty closed subscheme. If W_j is nonempty, apply the hyperplane avoidance claim to W_j to choose a hyperplane H_j that contains no irreducible component of W_j, and set W_{j+1} = W_j intersect H_j.

We claim that if W_{j+1} is nonempty then dim W_{j+1} <= dim W_j - 1. Let D be an irreducible component of W_{j+1}. Since W_{j+1} is closed in W_j, D is closed in W_j and is contained in an irreducible component C of W_j. Because H_j contains no irreducible component of W_j, D is a proper closed subset of C. In a noetherian finite-dimensional irreducible space, every proper closed subset has strictly smaller dimension: if a proper closed subset D had the same dimension as C, a maximal chain of irreducible closed subsets in D could be extended by C to a longer chain in C, contradiction. Therefore dim D < dim C <= dim W_j. Taking the supremum over all irreducible components D of W_{j+1} gives dim W_{j+1} <= dim W_j - 1.

By induction on j, if W_j is nonempty then dim W_j <= d - j. Since d <= r, the closed subscheme W_{r+1} cannot be nonempty, because a nonempty noetherian topological space has dimension at least 0. Hence the intersection of the underlying topological spaces of Z intersect H_0 intersect ... intersect H_r is empty.

For each i = 0,...,r, choose a linear form s_i in H^0(P^N,O(1)) defining H_i, and let s_i^Z be its restriction to Z. Let Z_i = V(s_i^Z) be the closed subscheme of Z defined by this section. Its underlying set is Z intersect H_i. By lemma_318 applied to the projective k-scheme Z, the ample line bundle L, the integer n = 1, and the section s_i^Z, the open subscheme U_i, namely the complement of Z_i in Z, is affine. The opens U_i cover Z: if a point z in Z were in none of the U_i, then z would belong to every Z_i, hence to the intersection of all Z intersect H_i, contradicting the emptiness just proved.

Finally, apply lemma_ordinary_vanishing_affine_cover to X = Z, e = r, and the affine open cover U_0,...,U_r. If some U_i is empty, discard it; the number m of remaining affine opens is at most r+1 and at least 1. The lemma gives H^n_et(Z,Q_ell) = 0 for every n > r + m - 1. Since r + m - 1 <= r + (r+1) - 1 = 2r, every n > 2r also satisfies n > r + m - 1. Thus H^n_et(Z,Q_ell) = 0 for all n > 2r. This completes the proof.

lemma_358_top_degree.statement: Let Q=p^a be a prime power, let X be a smooth projective geometrically connected variety of pure dimension d>=2 over F_Q, let k=overline{F}_Q, let ell != p be prime, let H be a very ample divisor on X defined over F_Q, and let xi in H^2_et(X_k,Q_ell) be the cycle class of H via a fixed nonzero element of Q_ell(1). Then cup product with xi^d is an isomorphism H^0_et(X_k,Q_ell) -> H^{2d}_et(X_k,Q_ell).
lemma_358_top_degree.proof:
Let F_0 = F_Q and k = overline F_Q. Fix once and for all the nonzero element of Q_ell(1) used in the statement. All cohomology groups below are of the base change to k, and for a closed subscheme Z of X_{F'} of pure codimension c defined over a finite extension F'/F_0 we write cl(Z) for its vector cycle class in H^{2c}_et(X_k,Q_ell), obtained from the usual cycle class in H^{2c}_et(X_k,Q_ell(c)) by using the fixed element of Q_ell(1); for finite sums of closed points this is extended additively. The class of H is xi.

1. Dimensions of the source and target. Since X is geometrically connected over F_0, X_k is connected. The etale H^0 of the constant sheaf Q_ell is the space of locally constant functions on X_k, hence is Q_ell with basis 1. Applying lemma_77(a) to X over F_0 (with m=1) gives a Q_ell-linear isomorphism tr_0: H^{2d}_et(X_k,Q_ell) -> Q_ell(-d), normalised by tr_0(cl(z)) = [kappa(z):F_0] for closed points z. Thus H^{2d}_et(X_k,Q_ell) is one-dimensional.

2. Construction of a curve whose class is a positive multiple of xi^{d-1}. Put X_0 = X over E_0 = F_0 and L_0 = O_X(H). We construct inductively smooth projective geometrically connected varieties X_r over finite fields E_r/F_0. Suppose X_{r-1} is smooth projective geometrically connected of pure dimension d-r+1 over E_{r-1}, and let L_{r-1} = O_X(H)|_{X_{r-1}}. This line bundle is ample and defined over E_{r-1}. Since d-r+1 >= 2, lemma_306 applies to X_{r-1}/E_{r-1} and L_{r-1}. It gives an integer n_r >= 1, a finite extension E_r/E_{r-1}, and a section of L_{r-1}^{tensor n_r} on X_{r-1,E_r} whose zero scheme X_r is an effective ample Cartier divisor, smooth and geometrically connected of pure dimension d-r over E_r. For r = d-1, C := X_{d-1} is a smooth projective geometrically connected curve over E_{d-1}.

We use the defining functoriality properties of the cycle class map for regular immersions: if i:Y -> X is a regular closed immersion, then i_*(1) = cl(Y); if D is a Cartier divisor on Y, then cl_Y(D) = c_1(O_Y(D)); and i_*(i^*alpha cup beta) = alpha cup i_*(beta). Applying these properties to the successive regular immersions X_r -> X_{r-1,E_r} -> ... -> X, and using that X_r is the zero scheme of a section of L_{r-1}^{tensor n_r}, we obtain inductively
  cl(X_r) = n_r xi cup cl(X_{r-1}).
Indeed, at the r-th step the class of X_r inside X_{r-1,E_r} is n_r i_r^*xi, and pushing forward to X gives n_r xi cup cl(X_{r-1}) by the projection formula. Hence, with N = n_1 ... n_{d-1}, we have
  cl(C) = N xi^{d-1} in H^{2d-2}_et(X_k,Q_ell).

3. An effective zero-cycle whose class is N xi^d. Let L_C = O_C(H). Since H is very ample on X, L_C is very ample on C. Choose a closed point z of C and put E = kappa(z). The base change C_E is a smooth projective geometrically connected curve over the finite field E, and z is an E-rational point of C_E. Because L_{C,E} is very ample, there exists a section s in H^0(C_E,L_{C,E}) which vanishes at z but is not identically zero on C_E: via a very ample embedding C_E -> P^N_E, choose a hyperplane through the image of z which does not contain C_E; such a hyperplane exists because otherwise C_E would be contained in the intersection of all hyperplanes through that point, namely a single point, contradicting dim C_E = 1.

Let Z = V(s) subset C_E. Since C_E is smooth and s is nonzero, Z is a nonempty effective Cartier divisor, hence a nonzero effective zero-cycle on X_E. Its class on C is cl_C(Z) = i_C^*xi, where i_C:C -> X is the closed immersion. By functoriality of cycle classes under proper pushforward and the projection formula,
  cl_X(Z) = cl_X(C) cup i_C^*xi = (N xi^{d-1}) cup xi = N xi^d.

4. Nonvanishing of xi^d. Apply lemma_77(a) to X_E, which is smooth projective geometrically connected of pure dimension d over the finite field E = F_Q^s for some s >= 1. It gives a trace isomorphism tr_E: H^{2d}_et(X_k,Q_ell) -> Q_ell(-d), normalised by tr_E(cl(z_0)) = [kappa(z_0):E] for closed points z_0 of X_E. Write the effective zero-cycle Z as sum m_nu z_nu, with m_nu positive integers. Additivity of cycle classes and the normalisation give
  tr_E(cl_X(Z)) = sum m_nu [kappa(z_nu):E],
viewed in Q_ell(-d) using the fixed trivialisation of Q_ell(1). This is a positive integer, hence nonzero in Q_ell(-d). Since cl_X(Z) = N xi^d and N is a positive integer, N tr_E(xi^d) is nonzero. As Q_ell has characteristic 0, tr_E(xi^d) is nonzero. Because tr_E is an isomorphism, xi^d is nonzero in H^{2d}_et(X_k,Q_ell).

5. Conclusion. The cup-product map Phi: H^0_et(X_k,Q_ell) -> H^{2d}_et(X_k,Q_ell), a |-> a cup xi^d, is Q_ell-linear. The domain is one-dimensional generated by 1, and Phi(1) = xi^d is nonzero. A nonzero linear map between one-dimensional vector spaces is an isomorphism. Therefore cup product with xi^d is an isomorphism.

lemma_369.statement: Let \(q=p^a\) be a prime power, let \(X\) be a smooth projective geometrically connected variety of pure dimension \(d\ge1\) over \(\mathbb F_q\), let \(k=\overline{\mathbb F}_q\), and let \(\ell\neq p\) be prime. Let \(H\) be an effective ample divisor on \(X\) defined over \(\mathbb F_q\), fix a nonzero element of \(\mathbb Q_\ell(1)\), let \(\xi\in H^2_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(X_k,\mathbb Q_\ell)\) be the cycle class of \(H\), and let \(L:H^n_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(X_k,\mathbb Q_\ell)\to H^{n+2}_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(X_k,\mathbb Q_\ell)\) be cup product with \(\xi\). For each \(n\ge0\) let \(F_n=(\mathrm{id}_{X_k}\times\operatorname{Spec}\sigma)^*\), \(\sigma(c)=c^q\), be the \(q\)-power arithmetic Frobenius of \(H^n_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(X_k,\mathbb Q_\ell)\). Then \(F_{n+2}\circ L = q\,(L\circ F_n)\) for every integer \(n\ge0\).
lemma_369.proof: Proof. Let f = (id_{X_k} times Spec sigma): X_k -> X_k be the q-power arithmetic Frobenius morphism, sigma(c)=c^q. By lemma_6a (user eoinm), the operator F_n in the statement is exactly the pullback f^* on H^n_{et}(X_k,Q_l) for every n. Let e in Q_l(1) be the fixed nonzero element, and let cl(H) in H^2_{et}(X_k,Q_l(1)) be the l-adic cycle class of H. The hypothesis that xi is the Q_l-coefficient cycle class of H via e means cl(H) = xi tensor e. Since H is an effective ample divisor defined over F_q, it is a codimension-one cycle on X defined over F_q. Lemma_78 (user eoinm) applied to this cycle says that the arithmetic Frobenius automorphism Phi^{(1)} of H^2_{et}(X_k,Q_l(1)) fixes cl(H), and that Phi^{(1)} corresponds to F_2 tensor (q^{-1} id) under the canonical identification H^2_{et}(X_k,Q_l(1)) = H^2_{et}(X_k,Q_l) tensor Q_l(1). Hence xi tensor e = cl(H) = Phi^{(1)}(cl(H)) = (F_2 xi) tensor (q^{-1} e) = (q^{-1} F_2 xi) tensor e. Because e is a nonzero element of the one-dimensional Q_l-vector space Q_l(1), tensoring with e is injective; therefore q^{-1} F_2(xi) = xi, i.e. F_2(xi)=q xi. Now fix n>=0 and alpha in H^n_{et}(X_k,Q_l). We use the convention L(alpha)=alpha cup xi; if the convention is L(alpha)=xi cup alpha, the same proof is identical with the order of the factors reversed. The cup product in etale cohomology is induced by the multiplication morphism mu: Q_l tensor Q_l -> Q_l of the constant sheaf. For any morphism f, pullback is symmetric monoidal and f^*Q_l=Q_l; consequently for all a in H^r and b in H^s one has f^*(a cup b)=f^*a cup f^*b. Applying this with a=alpha, b=xi, r=n, s=2 gives F_{n+2}(L(alpha)) = f^*(alpha cup xi) = f^*alpha cup f^*xi = F_n(alpha) cup F_2(xi). Using F_2(xi)=q xi and Q_l-bilinearity of cup product, this equals F_n(alpha) cup (q xi) = q (F_n(alpha) cup xi) = q L(F_n(alpha)). Thus (F_{n+2} circ L)(alpha) = (q L circ F_n)(alpha) for every alpha. Hence F_{n+2} circ L = q (L circ F_n) as Q_l-linear maps H^n_{et}(X_k,Q_l) -> H^{n+2}_{et}(X_k,Q_l). QED.

lemma_372.statement: Let \(q=p^a\) be a prime power and \(\ell\neq p\) prime, and let \(k=\overline{\mathbb F}_q\). Suppose that for every \(m\ge1\), every integer \(e\ge0\), and every smooth projective geometrically connected variety \(V\) of pure dimension \(e\) over \(\mathbb F_{q^m}\), the \(q^m\)-power arithmetic Frobenius is semisimple on \(H^e_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(V_k,\mathbb Q_\ell)\). Suppose also that for every \(m\ge1\), every smooth projective geometrically connected variety \(X'\) of pure dimension \(e'\ge2\) over \(\mathbb F_{q^m}\), every effective ample divisor \(Y'\subset X'\) defined over \(\mathbb F_{q^m}\), smooth and geometrically connected of pure dimension \(e'-1\), and \(U'=X'\setminus Y'\), one has \(H^j_{\mathrm{\acute et},c}(U'_k,\mathbb Q_\ell)=0\) for every integer \(j<e'\). Then for every smooth projective variety \(X\) over \(\mathbb F_q\), the \(q\)-power arithmetic Frobenius is semisimple on \(H^n_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(X_k,\mathbb Q_\ell)\) for every \(n\ge0\).
lemma_372.proof:
We fix q = p^a, ell != p, k = Fbar_q, and we assume throughout the two hypotheses of the lemma:
(A) for every m >= 1, every e >= 0 and every smooth projective geometrically connected variety V of pure dimension e over F_{q^m}, the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius is semisimple on H^e_et(V_k, Q_ell);
(B) for every m >= 1, every smooth projective geometrically connected X' of pure dimension e' >= 2 over F_{q^m}, every effective ample divisor Y' subset X' over F_{q^m} which is smooth and geometrically connected of pure dimension e'-1, and U' = X' \ Y', one has H^j_et,c(U'_k, Q_ell) = 0 for all j < e'.

Notation. For m >= 1 and a variety W over F_{q^m} we write F_{W,m} := (id_{W_k} x Spec sigma_m)^* for sigma_m(c) = c^{q^m}, the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius of H^n(W_k, Q_ell).

Step 0 (framework). By eoinm/lemma_45_finite_frob applied to the proper F_q-scheme X and K = Q_ell with its natural Frobenius structure, each H^n_et(X_k, Q_ell) is finite dimensional over Q_ell. By eoinm/lemma_6a, (id x Spec sigma)^* and (id x Spec sigma^{-1})^* are mutually inverse Q_ell-linear automorphisms of H^n_et(X_k, Q_ell); so "semisimple" is a statement about an invertible operator on a finite-dimensional space. By eoinm/lemma_5, for such an operator T, T is semisimple if and only if its base change to Qbar_ell is diagonalizable. We use the two formulations interchangeably; in particular the formulations of the cited lemmas (some say "semisimple", some say "diagonalizable over Qbar_ell") all agree.

Step 1 (the geometrically connected statement S(d)). For each integer d >= 0 we prove, by induction on d, the statement
S(d): for every m >= 1 and every smooth projective geometrically connected variety W of pure dimension d over F_{q^m}, the operator F_{W,m} is semisimple on H^n(W_k, Q_ell) for every n >= 0.

Case d = 0. W is smooth (hence etale) and projective over F_{q^m}, so W = Spec L with L/F_{q^m} finite separable; geometric connectedness forces L = F_{q^m} (if L = F_{q^{mr}} with r > 1 then L tensor k = k^r is disconnected). Thus W_k = Spec k. Since k is separably closed, Spec k is strictly henselian, every finite etale k-scheme is a disjoint union of copies of Spec k, and hence H^0(Spec k, Q_ell) = Q_ell while H^n(Spec k, Q_ell) = 0 for n >= 1 (the latter also follows from Spark/lemma_projective_top_degree_vanishing with d = 0). The pullback on the constant sheaf along id x Spec sigma_m is the identity on locally constant Q_ell-valued functions on a point, so F_{W,m} = id on Q_ell, which is diagonalizable; on the zero groups in higher degree the zero operator is trivially semisimple.

Case d = 1. This is exactly Spark/lemma_364 applied with q replaced by q^m: for every m >= 1 and every smooth projective geometrically connected curve C over F_{q^m}, F_{C,m} is diagonalizable over Qbar_ell on H^n(C_k, Q_ell) for every n >= 0.

Inductive step, d >= 2. Let W be smooth projective geometrically connected of pure dimension d over F_{q^m}; write F = F_{W,m}. We treat the degrees in four ranges.

(1a) n < d. We apply Spark/lemma_below_middle_induction with the role of "q" played by q^m, with e = d and with s = 1. Its first (vanishing) hypothesis reads: for every m' >= 1, every smooth projective geometrically connected X' of pure dimension e' >= 2 over F_{(q^m)^{m'}} = F_{q^{mm'}}, every effective ample divisor Y' over that field which is smooth and geometrically connected of dimension e'-1, and U' = X' \ Y', one has H^j_c(U'_k, Q_ell) = 0 for j < e'. This is precisely hypothesis (B) of the present lemma applied to mm' in place of m. Its second hypothesis reads: for every t >= 1 and every smooth projective geometrically connected V of pure dimension d-1 over F_{q^{mt}}, F_{V,mt} is semisimple on H^n(V_k, Q_ell) for 0 <= n <= d-1. This holds by the induction hypothesis S(d-1) applied to the field F_{q^{mt}} (which gives semisimplicity in every degree). The conclusion of lemma_below_middle_induction, with s = 1, is that for every smooth projective geometrically connected Z of pure dimension d over (q^m)^1 = F_{q^m} and every n < d, F_{Z,m} is semisimple on H^n(Z_k, Q_ell). Taking Z = W gives semisimplicity of F on H^n(W_k, Q_ell) for all n < d.

(1b) n = d. This is exactly hypothesis (A) applied to (m, e) = (m, d) and V = W.

(1c) n = d+1. Apply Spark/lemma_345 with q replaced by q^m and with n replaced by d-1 (valid since d >= 2 gives 0 <= d-1 <= d). It states that F is semisimple on H^{d-1}(W_k, Q_ell) if and only if it is semisimple on H^{2d-(d-1)}(W_k, Q_ell) = H^{d+1}(W_k, Q_ell). Since d-1 < d, semisimplicity on H^{d-1} holds by (1a); hence F is semisimple on H^{d+1}.

(1d) n > d+1. If n > 2d, then H^n(W_k, Q_ell) = 0 by Spark/lemma_projective_top_degree_vanishing applied to the projective k-scheme W_k of pure dimension d, and the zero operator on the zero space is semisimple. If d+2 <= n <= 2d, put n' = 2d - n; then 0 <= n' <= d-2 < d, so F is semisimple on H^{n'} by (1a), and lemma_345 (with q replaced by q^m, and with n replaced by n', which satisfies 0 <= n' <= d) gives that F is semisimple on H^{2d-n'} = H^n. 

The four ranges cover all n >= 0, completing the proof of S(d) and hence of S(d) for all d by induction.

Step 2 (reduction to a geometrically connected component). Let X be an arbitrary smooth projective variety over F_q. If X = empty, all cohomology groups vanish and there is nothing to prove. Since X is noetherian, it has finitely many connected components X_1, ..., X_r, each of which is open and closed in X; each X_alpha is therefore again smooth and projective over F_q, and being connected and smooth over a field it is of pure dimension d_alpha (the function x |-> dim_x X is locally constant on a smooth scheme, hence constant on X_alpha). As the X_alpha are open and closed, the X_alpha,k form a decomposition of X_k into open and closed subschemes, the etale topos of X_k is the product of the etale topoi of the (X_alpha)_k, and therefore
H^n(X_k, Q_ell) = oplus_{alpha=1}^{r} H^n((X_alpha)_k, Q_ell).
Moreover each (X_alpha)_k = X_alpha x_{F_q} k is stable under id x Spec sigma: on an affine open Spec B of X_alpha the map is B tensor_{F_q} k -> B tensor_{F_q} k, b tensor lambda |-> b tensor lambda^q, which lands in B tensor_{F_q} k. Hence F_{X,1} is the direct sum of the operators F_{X_alpha,1}, and by eoinm/lemma_9 it suffices to prove semisimplicity for each X_alpha. We thus fix alpha and rename X_alpha as X; X is connected, smooth, projective over F_q, of pure dimension d.

Claim. The automorphism id x Spec sigma of X_k permutes the connected components of X_k transitively.
Proof of the claim. X is smooth over the perfect field F_q, hence geometrically reduced, so X_k is reduced and its connected components Z_1, ..., Z_s coincide with its irreducible components; write Pi = {Z_1, ..., Z_s}. The group Gal(k/F_q) acts on the finite set Pi through id x Spec tau. Suppose the action is not transitive; write Pi = S disjoint union T with S, T nonempty and Gal-stable. Put Z_S = union_{Z_i in S} Z_i and Z_T = union_{Z_i in T} Z_i; both are closed and open in X_k and both are Gal-stable. A Gal-stable closed subscheme of X_k descends to a closed subscheme of X: the morphism X_k -> X is the base change of the faithfully flat morphism Spec k -> Spec F_q, closed immersions satisfy effective fpqc descent (they are affine), and the canonical descent datum on Z_S (the identification of its two pullbacks to X_k x_X X_k coming from Galois invariance of the underlying set) is effective. We obtain closed subschemes W, W' subset X with W_k = Z_S and W'_k = Z_T. Both W and W' are nonempty (each Z_i is nonempty) and both are proper in X (their base change to k is a proper closed subset, and being a proper closed subscheme can be checked after the faithfully flat base change Spec k -> Spec F_q). Moreover W union W' = X, since (W union W')_k = Z_S union Z_T = X_k and equality of closed subschemes of X can be checked after faithfully flat base change. Thus the underlying space of X is the union of two proper nonempty closed subsets, contradicting the connectedness of X. Hence Gal(k/F_q) acts transitively on Pi. Finally Gal(k/F_q) ~ = Zhat is topologically generated by sigma: c |-> c^q, and the permutation representation on the finite set Pi is continuous with finite image, so transitivity of the whole group implies transitivity of the cyclic subgroup generated by sigma. That is exactly transitivity of id x Spec sigma on the components of X_k. End of claim.

We now apply Spark/lemma_343 to X. It gives: for one component X_0 of X_k and m >= 1 minimal with (id x Spec sigma^m)(X_0) = X_0, semisimplicity of the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius on H^n(X_0, Q_ell) for every n >= 0 implies semisimplicity of F_{X,1} on H^n(X_k, Q_ell) for every n >= 0. It therefore remains to identify X_0 with the base change of a smooth projective geometrically connected variety over F_{q^m}, compatibly with Frobenius, and to invoke S(d).

Descent of X_0. Choose a closed immersion j: X -> P^N_{F_q} (X is projective over F_q). Then X_0 is a closed subscheme of P^N_k cut out by a homogeneous ideal I subset k[x_0, ..., x_N]. The automorphism Phi := id x Spec sigma^m of P^N_k acts on the homogeneous coordinate ring by applying sigma^m to the coefficients, and the condition Phi(X_0) = X_0 is equivalent to sigma^m(I) = I. Choose r >= 1 such that I is generated by homogeneous polynomials with coefficients in E := F_{q^{mr}} (possible since I is finitely generated); then sigma^m(E) = E and J := I cap E[x] satisfies J tensor_E k = I. The ring map F_{q^m}[x] -> E[x] is faithfully flat (E is free of finite rank over F_{q^m}), and E/F_{q^m} is finite Galois with group G = <sigma^m|_E>; Galois descent for modules over the polynomial ring (equivalence between F_{q^m}[x]-modules and E[x]-modules with semilinear G-action) identifies G-stable E[x]-submodules of E[x] with ideals of F_{q^m}[x]. Since sigma^m(J) = J, there is a unique ideal J_0 := J cap F_{q^m}[x] = I cap F_{q^m}[x] subset F_{q^m}[x] with J = J_0 tensor_{F_{q^m}} E. Let Z subset P^N_{F_{q^m}} be the closed subscheme defined by J_0. Then Z_k = V(J_0 tensor_{F_{q^m}} k) = V(I) = X_0 as closed subschemes of P^N_k.

Properties of Z. Z is projective over F_{q^m} (closed in P^N). Smoothness of Z -> Spec F_{q^m} may be checked after the faithfully flat base change Spec k -> Spec F_{q^m}; but Z_k = X_0 is a connected component of the smooth k-scheme X_k, hence open in X_k, hence smooth over k. Thus Z is smooth over F_{q^m}. It is of pure dimension d, since X_0 is an irreducible component of the pure d-dimensional scheme X_k. It is geometrically connected, since Z x_{F_{q^m}} kbar = Z_k = X_0 (k is already algebraically closed) is connected. Finally, under the identification Z_k = X_0, the operator (id_{Z_k} x Spec sigma_m)^* of lemma_343 is precisely the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius F_{Z,m} of Z, because (id x Spec sigma^m) preserves Z_k (it acts on k[x] by sigma^m on coefficients and fixes F_{q^m}[x] pointwise, so it preserves J_0 tensor k) and restricts to the defining morphism of F_{Z,m}.

Conclusion of Step 2. By S(d) applied to the smooth projective geometrically connected F_{q^m}-variety Z of pure dimension d, the operator F_{Z,m} is semisimple on H^n(Z_k, Q_ell) = H^n(X_0, Q_ell) for every n >= 0. Lemma_343 then gives that F_{X,1} is semisimple on H^n(X_k, Q_ell) for every n >= 0.

Step 3 (end of proof). Applying Step 2 to each connected component X_alpha of the original X and reassembling with eoinm/lemma_9 (Step 1 of the reduction, in reverse), the q-power arithmetic Frobenius F_{X,1} = oplus_alpha F_{X_alpha,1} is semisimple on H^n(X_k, Q_ell) for every n >= 0. Since X was an arbitrary smooth projective variety over F_q, this is exactly the desired conclusion. QED.

lemma_373.statement: Let \(q=p^a\) be a prime power, let \(C\) be a smooth projective curve over \(\mathbb F_q\), let \(k=\overline{\mathbb F}_q\), and let \(\ell\neq p\) be prime. Then the \(q\)-power arithmetic Frobenius \((\mathrm{id}_{C_k}\times\operatorname{Spec}\sigma)^*\), \(\sigma(c)=c^q\), is semisimple on \(H^n_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(C_k,\mathbb Q_\ell)\) for every integer \(n\ge0\).
lemma_373.proof:
Proof of lemma_373.

Fix k = \overline{\mathbb F}_q and write \sigma:k\to k, \sigma(c)=c^q, for the q-power field automorphism. Put
\[ F := (\mathrm{id}_{C_k}\times \operatorname{Spec}\sigma)^* ,\]
the q-power arithmetic Frobenius operator on the cohomology of C_k.

Step 0 (Generalities). By lemma_6a (eoinm), for every n\ge 0 the pullback F is a \mathbb Q_\ell-linear automorphism of H^n_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(C_k,\mathbb Q_\ell) (its inverse is the geometric Frobenius (id\times\operatorname{Spec}\sigma^{-1})^*). By lemma_45_finite_frob (eoinm), applied to the proper \mathbb F_q-scheme C and to the constant sheaf \mathbb Q_\ell equipped with its natural arithmetic Frobenius isomorphism \psi:F_C^*\mathbb Q_\ell\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbb Q_\ell, each H^n_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(C_k,\mathbb Q_\ell) is finite-dimensional over \mathbb Q_\ell. By lemma_5 (eoinm), an operator on a finite-dimensional \mathbb Q_\ell-space is semisimple if and only if it is diagonalizable over \overline{\mathbb Q}_\ell; we use the two formulations interchangeably.

If C=\varnothing then every H^n_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(C_k,\mathbb Q_\ell) is the zero space, on which the (unique) operator is diagonalizable; assume henceforth C\neq\varnothing.

Step 1 (Reduction to the connected components of C over \mathbb F_q). Since C is noetherian, it is a finite disjoint union C = \bigsqcup_{j=1}^{s} C_j of its connected components, each C_j open and closed in C. Each C_j is smooth (open subscheme of the smooth \mathbb F_q-scheme C), projective (closed subscheme of the projective \mathbb F_q-scheme C), non-empty, and of pure dimension 1 (open subscheme of a smooth scheme of relative dimension 1). Base change preserves disjoint unions of open-and-closed subschemes, so C_k = \bigsqcup_{j=1}^{s} C_{j,k}. For the \acute etale topos, a sheaf on a finite disjoint union is a tuple of sheaves on the pieces, and cohomology of a finite disjoint union is the product of the cohomologies; since the product is finite, for each n we have a canonical isomorphism
\[ H^n_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(C_k,\mathbb Q_\ell) \;\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\ \prod_{j=1}^{s} H^n_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(C_{j,k},\mathbb Q_\ell) \;=\ \bigoplus_{j=1}^{s} H^n_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(C_{j,k},\mathbb Q_\ell). \]
Because each C_j is defined over \mathbb F_q, the morphism \mathrm{id}\times\operatorname{Spec}\sigma preserves C_{j,k}, and under the above identification F = \bigoplus_j F_j where F_j := (\mathrm{id}_{C_{j,k}}\times\operatorname{Spec}\sigma)^* is the operator attached to C_j (restriction to components commutes with pullback along a morphism preserving components). All spaces are finite-dimensional (Step 0) and all F_j are invertible (Step 0), so lemma_9 (eoinm) applies: \bigoplus_j F_j is semisimple if and only if each F_j is. It therefore suffices to prove the statement for each C_j, and we may from now on assume that C is connected.

Step 2 (For C connected, F permutes the connected components of C_k transitively). Since C is proper over \mathbb F_q, B := \Gamma(C,\mathcal O_C) is a finite-dimensional \mathbb F_q-algebra (finiteness of cohomology of coherent sheaves on a proper scheme over a field); C is reduced and connected, so \Gamma(C,\mathcal O_C) is a product of fields indexed by the connected components, hence a field: B/\mathbb F_q is a finite field extension. Flat base change for the quasi-compact separated structure morphism gives
\[ A := \Gamma(C_k,\mathcal O_{C_k}) \;=\; B\otimes_{\mathbb F_q} k. \]
Since \mathbb F_q is perfect, B/\mathbb F_q is finite separable, and since k is algebraically closed, evaluation gives an isomorphism of k-algebras
\[ A \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ } \prod_{\tau\in \operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb F_q}(B,k)} k,\qquad b\otimes\lambda \longmapsto \big(\tau(b)\lambda\big)_\tau , \]
so A \cong k^{[B:\mathbb F_q]}.

On the other hand, let W_1,\dots,W_r be the connected components of C_k: they are finite in number and open and closed because C_k is noetherian. Each W_\nu is proper over k (closed in the proper C_k), reduced (open in the reduced C_k) and connected, so \Gamma(W_\nu,\mathcal O) is a finite field extension of the algebraically closed field k, hence equals k. As C_k = \bigsqcup_\nu W_\nu we get A = \prod_\nu \Gamma(W_\nu,\mathcal O) \cong k^{r}, and the primitive idempotents of A are exactly the characteristic functions e_\nu of the W_\nu. Comparing the two descriptions of A gives r = [B:\mathbb F_q], and the primitive idempotents of A are in bijection with the embeddings \tau:B\hookrightarrow k; write e_\tau for the idempotent characterised by
\[ \varphi_{\tau'}(e_\tau)=\delta_{\tau,\tau'},\qquad \varphi_\tau:A\to k,\ \ \varphi_\tau(b\otimes\lambda)=\tau(b)\lambda . \]

The morphism F = \mathrm{id}_B\otimes\operatorname{Spec}\sigma acts on A by F^*(b\otimes\lambda)=b\otimes\lambda^q. For each \tau' the composite \varphi_{\tau'}\circ F^*:A\to k, \ b\otimes\lambda\mapsto \tau'(b)\lambda^q, is a ring homomorphism, and one checks directly that
\[ \varphi_{\tau'}\circ F^* \;=\; \sigma\circ\varphi_{\sigma^{-1}\circ\tau'} \]
since the right-hand side sends b\otimes\lambda to \sigma(\sigma^{-1}(\tau'(b))\lambda)=\tau'(b)\lambda^q. Therefore
\[ \varphi_{\tau'}\big(F^*(e_\tau)\big)=\sigma\big(\varphi_{\sigma^{-1}\circ\tau'}(e_\tau)\big)=\sigma(\delta_{\sigma^{-1}\circ\tau',\,\tau})=\delta_{\tau',\,\sigma\circ\tau}, \]
because \sigma^{-1}\circ\tau'=\tau \Longleftrightarrow \tau'=\sigma\circ\tau, and \sigma(0)=0,\ \sigma(1)=1. Hence F^*(e_\tau)=e_{\sigma\circ\tau}: F permutes the connected components of C_k, and the induced permutation of the index set \operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb F_q}(B,k) is \tau\mapsto\sigma\circ\tau. Now \operatorname{Gal}(B/\mathbb F_q) acts simply transitively on \operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb F_q}(B,k), and the restriction to B of \sigma(c)=c^q is exactly the Frobenius generator x\mapsto x^q of the cyclic group \operatorname{Gal}(B/\mathbb F_q). Hence the cyclic group \langle\sigma\rangle alone acts transitively on \operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb F_q}(B,k). Conclusion: the q-power arithmetic Frobenius permutes the connected components of C_k transitively.

Step 3 (Descent of one geometric component to \mathbb F_{q^m}). Let X_0 be one of the components W_\nu and let m\ge 1 be minimal with F^m(X_0)=X_0 (m is the orbit size, here m=[B:\mathbb F_q]). Let e\in A be the idempotent of X_0. Set K:=\mathbb F_{q^m} and \tau:=\sigma^m, \tau(c)=c^{q^m}; \tau topologically generates \operatorname{Gal}(k/K). Since F^{m} = (\mathrm{id}\times\operatorname{Spec}\sigma)^m = \mathrm{id}\times\operatorname{Spec}\sigma^m (composition of morphisms over \sigma multiplies the field maps) and F^m(X_0)=X_0, the idempotent e is fixed by the \tau-semilinear automorphism F^{m*} of A. Put M := \Gamma(C_K,\mathcal O_{C_K}) = B\otimes_{\mathbb F_q} K; flat base change identifies A = M\otimes_K k, and under this identification F^{m*} = \mathrm{id}_M\otimes\tau. For the Galois extension k/K one has (M\otimes_K k)^{\operatorname{Gal}(k/K)} = M: indeed M\to (M\otimes_K k) \rightrightarrows M\otimes_K k\otimes_K k is the faithfully flat descent equalizer, and identifying M\otimes_K k\otimes_K k \cong \operatorname{Map}_{\mathrm{cont}}(\operatorname{Gal}(k/K),\,k) by a\otimes b\mapsto (g\mapsto a\,g(b)) turns the two structure maps into the two projections, so the equalizer is exactly the \operatorname{Gal}(k/K)-invariant submodule. The \tau-orbit of e consists of the single point e, and the action of \operatorname{Gal}(k/K) on the finite set of idempotents of A factors through the finite cyclic quotient generated by \tau; hence e is fixed by all of \operatorname{Gal}(k/K) and e\in M. An idempotent of \Gamma(C_K,\mathcal O_{C_K}) is the same datum as an open-and-closed subscheme of C_K, so there exists a unique open-and-closed subscheme Z\subset C_K with Z_k = X_0.

This Z is a smooth projective geometrically connected curve over K=\mathbb F_{q^m}: it is smooth and of pure dimension 1 because it is open in the smooth pure-dimensional K-scheme C_K; it is projective over K because it is closed in the K-projective scheme C_K; it is non-empty and geometrically connected because Z_k = X_0 is a connected component of C_k.

Step 4 (Identification of the operator on X_0). As noted above F^m = \mathrm{id}_{C_k}\times\operatorname{Spec}\tau. Since X_0 is F^m-stable, the restriction of F^m to X_0 is the morphism (\mathrm{id}_{X_0}\times\operatorname{Spec}\tau). Under the identification X_0 = Z_k of Step 3, this morphism is precisely the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius morphism of Z_k attached to the \mathbb F_{q^m}-model Z: it is the base change to k of the relative q^m-power Frobenius on \operatorname{Spec}\mathbb F_{q^m}, paired with the identity on Z. Consequently, on H^n_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(X_0,\mathbb Q_\ell) the operator (\mathrm{id}_{X_0}\times\operatorname{Spec}\tau)^* is exactly the operator (\mathrm{id}_{Z_k}\times\operatorname{Spec}\sigma)^*, \sigma(c)=c^{q^m}, appearing in lemma_364.

Step 5 (Conclusion when C is connected). Apply lemma_364 (Spark) to the prime power q=p^a, to the integer m\ge 1, and to the smooth projective geometrically connected curve Z over \mathbb F_{q^m}: the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius is semisimple (diagonalizable over \overline{\mathbb Q}_\ell) on H^n_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(Z_k,\mathbb Q_\ell)=H^n_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(X_0,\mathbb Q_\ell) for every n\ge 0. By Step 4 this is precisely the hypothesis of lemma_343 (Spark) for X:=C (a smooth projective variety over \mathbb F_q), for the component X_0, and for the integer m; the other hypotheses of lemma_343 (transitive permutation of the connected components of C_k by F, minimality of m) were verified in Steps 2 and 3. Lemma_343 then yields that F is semisimple on H^n_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(C_k,\mathbb Q_\ell) for every n\ge 0.

Step 6 (End of the proof). Returning to a possibly disconnected C, Step 5 applied to each connected component C_j shows that every F_j is semisimple on H^n_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(C_{j,k},\mathbb Q_\ell). By lemma_9 (eoinm), the direct-sum operator F=\bigoplus_j F_j is semisimple on H^n_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(C_k,\mathbb Q_\ell)=\bigoplus_j H^n_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(C_{j,k},\mathbb Q_\ell). By lemma_5 this is the desired semisimplicity, for every integer n\ge 0. \qed

Remarks on edge cases. (i) By lemma_projective_top_degree_vanishing applied to the projective k-scheme C_k of pure dimension 1, H^n_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(C_k,\mathbb Q_\ell)=0 for n>2, so in those degrees the assertion concerns the zero operator on the zero space and is vacuous; the argument above covers all n uniformly.
(ii) If one's convention allows a "curve" to have 0-dimensional connected components, the same conclusion holds for such a component D: then D=\operatorname{Spec} E with E/\mathbb F_q finite separable, D_k is a finite discrete set, H^n_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(D_k,\mathbb Q_\ell)=0 for n>0 by lemma_projective_top_degree_vanishing with d=0, and H^0_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(D_k,\mathbb Q_\ell)=\operatorname{Map}(D_k(k),\mathbb Q_\ell) with F acting by permutation of the basis of characteristic functions of points. Taking m a common multiple of the orbit lengths, F^m fixes every point and acts as the identity on \mathbb Q_\ell, so F^m=\mathrm{id} on H^0; the minimal polynomial of F therefore divides T^m-1, which is separable over \mathbb Q_\ell (characteristic 0), so F is semisimple on H^0 and trivially on the vanishing groups.

lemma_375.statement: Let \(q=p^a\) be a prime power and \(\ell\neq p\) prime, let \(Y\) be a smooth projective geometrically connected variety over \(\mathbb F_q\), let \(\mathcal E\) be a vector bundle of rank \(r+1\ge1\) on \(Y\) defined over \(\mathbb F_q\), let \(\pi:\mathbb P=\operatorname{Proj}(\operatorname{Sym}_{\mathcal O_Y}\mathcal E)\to Y\) be the projective bundle of one-dimensional quotients, and let \(k=\overline{\mathbb F}_q\). If the \(q\)-power arithmetic Frobenius is semisimple on \(H^n_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(Y_k,\mathbb Q_\ell)\) for every \(n\ge0\), then the \(q\)-power arithmetic Frobenius is semisimple on \(H^n_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(\mathbb P_k,\mathbb Q_\ell)\) for every \(n\ge0\).
lemma_375.proof:
Let F_Y and F_P denote the q-power arithmetic Frobenius automorphisms (id times Spec sigma)^*, sigma(u)=u^q, on H^m_et(Y_k,Q_l) and H^n_et(P_k,Q_l). The variety P is defined over F_q because E is defined over F_q; Y is projective over F_q, hence proper.
Fix n>=0. By lemma_45_finite_frob applied to the proper F_q-variety Y and the constant sheaf Q_l on Y_k with its natural arithmetic Frobenius isomorphism (the constant sheaf is constructible), every H^m_et(Y_k,Q_l) is finite-dimensional over Q_l. For m<0 set H^m_et(Y_k,Q_l)=0. For each i with 0<=i<=r and n-2i>=0 put W_i=H^{n-2i}_et(Y_k,Q_l), and let J_n be the finite set of such i for which W_i is nonzero. Define V_n=direct sum_{i in J_n} W_i. This is a finite-dimensional Q_l-vector space.
By lemma_307, the projective-bundle map alpha_n from the full direct sum over i=0,...,r of H^{n-2i}_et(Y_k,Q_l) to H^n_et(P_k,Q_l), (x_i) -> sum_i pi^*x_i cup c^i, is a Q_l-linear isomorphism, and it carries the operator direct sum_i q^i F_Y to F_P. Since the omitted summands are zero, alpha_n restricts to a Q_l-linear isomorphism alpha_n: V_n -> H^n_et(P_k,Q_l). Define T_n on V_n by T_n((x_i)_{i in J_n})=(q^i F_Y x_i)_{i in J_n}. The equivariance in lemma_307 says alpha_n(T_n(v))=F_P(alpha_n(v)) for all v in V_n. In particular H^n_et(P_k,Q_l) is finite-dimensional.
If V_n=0, then alpha_n identifies H^n_et(P_k,Q_l) with the zero vector space; the unique operator on the zero vector space is diagonalizable (empty eigenbasis), so the conclusion holds. Assume now V_n is nonzero.
For each i in J_n, W_i is nonzero finite-dimensional. Since n-2i>=0, the hypothesis gives semisimplicity of F_Y on W_i. The integer q^i is a nonzero element of Q_l because q=p^a and l != p. By lemma_5, semisimplicity of F_Y on W_i is equivalent to diagonalizability of F_Y tensor Q_lbar on W_i tensor Q_lbar. Choose an eigenbasis e_j of W_i tensor Q_lbar for F_Y, with eigenvalues lambda_j. Then (q^i F_Y) tensor Q_lbar sends e_j to q^i lambda_j e_j, hence is diagonalizable. By lemma_5 again, q^i F_Y is semisimple on W_i.
By lemma_6a, F_Y is a Q_l-linear automorphism of each H^m_et(Y_k,Q_l); since q^i is nonzero, q^i F_Y is invertible on each W_i. Therefore lemma_9 applies to the finite direct sum V_n and shows that T_n is semisimple.
Again by lemma_6a, F_P is a Q_l-linear automorphism of H^n_et(P_k,Q_l), and T_n is invertible. The isomorphism alpha_n is equivariant: alpha_n T_n = F_P alpha_n. Hence lemma_8 applies, and semisimplicity of T_n implies semisimplicity of F_P on H^n_et(P_k,Q_l).
Since n was arbitrary, F_P is semisimple on H^n_et(P_k,Q_l) for every n>=0.

lemma_377.statement: Let \(q=p^a\) be a prime power, let \(\ell\neq p\) be prime, let \(X\) be a smooth projective variety over \(\mathbb F_q\), let \(k=\overline{\mathbb F}_q\), and let \(j\ge0\) be an integer. Fix a nonzero element of \(\mathbb Q_\ell(j)\), and for a closed integral subscheme \(Z_0\subseteq X_{\mathbb F_{q^r}}\) of codimension \(j\) let \(\mathrm{cl}(Z_0)\in H^{2j}_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(X_k,\mathbb Q_\ell)\) be the unique vector whose tensor with that element is the \(\ell\)-adic cycle class of the base change of \(Z_0\) to \(X_k\). Suppose there exists an integer \(r\ge1\) such that \(H^{2j}_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(X_k,\mathbb Q_\ell)\) is spanned over \(\mathbb Q_\ell\) by classes \(\mathrm{cl}(Z_{0,i})\) of closed integral subschemes \(Z_{0,i}\subseteq X_{\mathbb F_{q^r}}\) of codimension \(j\). Then the \(q\)-power arithmetic Frobenius \((\mathrm{id}_{X_k}\times\operatorname{Spec}\sigma)^*\), \(\sigma(c)=c^q\), is semisimple on \(H^{2j}_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(X_k,\mathbb Q_\ell)\).
lemma_377.proof:
We write $F:=(\mathrm{id}_{X_k}\times\operatorname{Spec}\sigma)^*$, $\sigma(c)=c^q$, for the $q$-power arithmetic Frobenius, and $V:=H^{2j}_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(X_k,\mathbb Q_\ell)$; we must show that $T:=F|_V$ is semisimple (i.e. diagonalizable over $\overline{\mathbb Q}_\ell$).

**Step 1: $V$ is finite dimensional and $T$ is a $\mathbb Q_\ell$-linear automorphism.**
Since $X$ is smooth projective over $\mathbb F_q$, it is proper. Apply lemma_45_finite_frob (eoinm) with $K=\mathbb Q_\ell[0]\in D^b_c(X_k,\mathbb Q_\ell)$, which is proper over $\mathbb F_q$, equipped with its natural arithmetic Frobenius isomorphism $\psi:F_X^*\mathbb Q_\ell\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbb Q_\ell$. The lemma gives that $H^{2j}(X_k,\mathbb Q_\ell)=H^{2j}_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(X_k,\mathbb Q_\ell)$ is finite dimensional over $\mathbb Q_\ell$. Lemma_6a (eoinm), applied to the scheme $X$ over $\mathbb F_q$ with $i=2j$, gives that $F_{\mathrm{ar}}=(\mathrm{id}_X\times\sigma)^*$ is a $\mathbb Q_\ell$-linear automorphism of $H^{2j}_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(X_k,\mathbb Q_\ell)$ (and equals the inverse of geometric Frobenius). Thus $T$ is a well-defined invertible $\mathbb Q_\ell$-linear operator on the finite-dimensional space $V$. This is exactly the operator appearing in the statement.

**Step 2: the spanning classes are eigenvectors of $T^r$.**
By hypothesis there is an integer $r\ge1$ and a family $\{Z_{0,i}\}_{i\in I}$ of closed integral subschemes $Z_{0,i}\subseteq X_{\mathbb F_{q^r}}$ of codimension $j$ such that $\{\mathrm{cl}(Z_{0,i})\}_{i\in I}$ spans $V$ over $\mathbb Q_\ell$. (If $I=\varnothing$ then $V=0$ and there is nothing to prove; assume $I\neq\varnothing$.)

Each $Z_{0,i}$ is integral, hence has exactly one irreducible component, namely itself, whose codimension in $X_{\mathbb F_{q^r}}$ is $j$; so $Z_{0,i}$ is automatically of *pure* codimension $j$. Therefore lemma_314 (Spark) applies with $m=r$ and with the fixed nonzero element of $\mathbb Q_\ell(j)$ of the statement playing the role of $\xi$: for every $i\in I$,
\[
T^{r}\bigl(\mathrm{cl}(Z_{0,i})\bigr)=F^{r}\bigl(\mathrm{cl}(Z_{0,i})\bigr)=q^{rj}\,\mathrm{cl}(Z_{0,i}).
\]

**Step 3: $T^r$ is the scalar $q^{rj}$.**
Put $c:=q^{rj}\in\mathbb Q_\ell^{\times}$ (a positive rational number, hence nonzero). Both $T^r$ and $c\,\mathrm{id}_V$ are $\mathbb Q_\ell$-linear endomorphisms of $V$ which agree on the spanning set $\{\mathrm{cl}(Z_{0,i})\}_{i\in I}$; by $\mathbb Q_\ell$-linearity they agree on all of $V$. Hence with
\[
P(t):=t^{r}-c\in\mathbb Q_\ell[t]\subseteq\overline{\mathbb Q}_\ell[t],\qquad P(T)=T^{r}-c\,\mathrm{id}_V=0.
\]

**Step 4: $P$ splits over $\overline{\mathbb Q}_\ell$ into $r$ distinct linear factors, and $T$ becomes diagonalizable after scalar extension.**
Let $W:=V\otimes_{\mathbb Q_\ell}\overline{\mathbb Q}_\ell$ and $T_W:=T\otimes\mathrm{id}$; then $P(T_W)=0$ as well. Since $\overline{\mathbb Q}_\ell$ is algebraically closed of characteristic $0$ and $c\neq0$, $P$ has $r$ pairwise distinct roots $\zeta_1,\dots,\zeta_r\in\overline{\mathbb Q}_\ell^{\times}$: a repeated root would be a common zero of $P$ and $P'(t)=r\,t^{r-1}$ (valid since $r\neq0$ in characteristic $0$), the only zero of $P'$ is $0$, and $P(0)=-c\neq0$. Thus $P(t)=\prod_{b=1}^{r}(t-\zeta_b)$.

For each $a\in\{1,\dots,r\}$ define the Lagrange polynomial
\[
Q_a(t):=\prod_{b\neq a}\frac{t-\zeta_b}{\zeta_a-\zeta_b}\in\overline{\mathbb Q}_\ell[t]
\]
(with the empty-product convention $Q_1(t)=1$ when $r=1$). We record two identities.

*(a)* $\displaystyle\sum_{a=1}^{r}Q_a(t)=1$ in $\overline{\mathbb Q}_\ell[t]$. Indeed, each $Q_a$ has degree $\le r-1$ and satisfies $Q_a(\zeta_b)=\delta_{ab}$ (the factor $b=a$ is present in the numerator of $Q_a$ exactly when $b\ne a$). Hence both sides of (a) are polynomials of degree $\le r-1$ taking the same value $\delta$ at the $r$ distinct points $\zeta_1,\dots,\zeta_r$; their difference has degree $\le r-1$ with $r$ roots, so it is zero.

*(b)* $\displaystyle (t-\zeta_a)\,Q_a(t)=\frac{P(t)}{\prod_{b\neq a}(\zeta_a-\zeta_b)}$ in $\overline{\mathbb Q}_\ell[t]$. Indeed, $(t-\zeta_a)Q_a(t)$ is a polynomial of degree $r$ (its leading coefficient is $1/\prod_{b\neq a}(\zeta_a-\zeta_b)\neq0$, since $Q_a$ is monic of degree $r-1$ up to that scalar). It vanishes at every root of $P$: at $t=\zeta_a$ because of the factor $t-\zeta_a$, and at $t=\zeta_b$ for $b\ne a$ because $t-\zeta_b$ is a factor of $Q_a$. Since the $\zeta_b$ are $r$ distinct roots, $(t-\zeta_a)Q_a(t)=\lambda\prod_b(t-\zeta_b)=\lambda P(t)$ with $\lambda=1/\prod_{b\neq a}(\zeta_a-\zeta_b)$ by comparison of leading coefficients, which is the claimed identity. (Note that it is $(t-\zeta_a)Q_a(t)$ itself, not $(t-\zeta_a)Q_a(t)-1$, that is divisible by $P$; the latter takes the constant value $-1$ at every $\zeta_b$.)

Specialising $t$ to $T_W$ in (b) and using $P(T_W)=0$ gives, for every $a$,
\[
(T_W-\zeta_a)\,Q_a(T_W)=\Bigl(\prod_{b\neq a}(\zeta_a-\zeta_b)\Bigr)^{-1}P(T_W)=0,
\]
so $\mathrm{im}\,Q_a(T_W)\subseteq\ker(T_W-\zeta_a)$.

Now take any $w\in W$. By (a), $w=\sum_{a=1}^r w_a$ with $w_a:=Q_a(T_W)w\in\ker(T_W-\zeta_a)$. Hence $W=\sum_{a}\ker(T_W-\zeta_a)$.

The sum is direct: suppose $\sum_a w_a=0$ with $w_a\in\ker(T_W-\zeta_a)$. For a fixed $b$, first note that if $v\in\ker(T_W-\zeta)$ then $T_W^{n}v=\zeta^{n}v$ for all $n\ge0$ (induction), hence $R(T_W)v=R(\zeta)v$ for every $R\in\overline{\mathbb Q}_\ell[t]$. Applying $Q_b(T_W)$: for $a\ne b$, $t-\zeta_a$ divides $Q_b$, so $Q_b(T_W)w_a=Q_b(\zeta_a)w_a=0$; and $Q_b(T_W)w_b=Q_b(\zeta_b)w_b=w_b$ since $Q_b(\zeta_b)=1$. Thus $0=Q_b(T_W)\bigl(\sum_a w_a\bigr)=w_b$. So every $w_b$ vanishes and the sum is direct:
\[
W=\bigoplus_{a=1}^{r}\ker(T_W-\zeta_a).
\]
Choosing a basis of each $\ker(T_W-\zeta_a)$ and concatenating gives a basis of $W$ consisting of eigenvectors of $T_W$; i.e. $T_W$ is diagonalizable over $\overline{\mathbb Q}_\ell$.

**Step 5: descent to $V$.**
By lemma_5 (eoinm), applied to the finite-dimensional $\mathbb Q_\ell$-vector space $V$ and the operator $T$, $T$ is semisimple on $V$ if and only if $T_W=T\otimes\mathrm{id}$ is diagonalizable on $V\otimes_{\mathbb Q_\ell}\overline{\mathbb Q}_\ell$. Step 4 establishes the right-hand side, so $T=F|_{H^{2j}_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(X_k,\mathbb Q_\ell)}$ is semisimple.

This is precisely the required conclusion: the $q$-power arithmetic Frobenius $(\mathrm{id}_{X_k}\times\operatorname{Spec}\sigma)^*$ is semisimple on $H^{2j}_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(X_k,\mathbb Q_\ell)$. $\blacksquare$

lemma_380.statement: Let q=p^a be a prime power, let ℓ≠p be prime, let X and Y be smooth projective geometrically connected varieties of pure dimension d over F_q, and let f:Y→X be a surjective generically finite morphism of degree prime to ℓ. Let k=overline(F_q). If the q-power arithmetic Frobenius is semisimple, equivalently diagonalizable over overline(Q_ℓ), on H^n_{et}(Y_k,Q_ℓ) for every integer n≥0, then the q-power arithmetic Frobenius is semisimple on H^n_{et}(X_k,Q_ℓ) for every integer n≥0.
lemma_380.proof: Fix an integer n >= 0. Let k = overline{F}_q and let sigma(c)=c^q. Write F_X = id_{X_k} times Spec sigma and F_Y = id_{Y_k} times Spec sigma for the q-power arithmetic Frobenius morphisms, and write Phi_X = F_X^* and Phi_Y = F_Y^* for the induced Q_ell-linear operators on H^n_et(X_k,Q_ell) and H^n_et(Y_k,Q_ell). We prove that Phi_X is semisimple. First suppose d=0. Then X and Y are zero-dimensional smooth projective geometrically connected F_q-varieties. A zero-dimensional finite type scheme over a field is finite, and smoothness implies that X and Y are finite etale over F_q. Base change to k turns a finite etale algebra over F_q into a finite product of copies of Spec k; geometric connectedness forces there to be exactly one copy. Hence X_k = Y_k = Spec k and X = Y = Spec F_q. For n=0, H^0_et(Spec k,Q_ell)=Q_ell, and the pullback of the constant sheaf Q_ell along Spec sigma induces the identity on global sections, so Phi_X is the identity and is semisimple. For n>0, X_k is a projective k-scheme of pure dimension 0, so lemma_projective_top_degree_vanishing gives H^n_et(X_k,Q_ell)=0; the zero operator on the zero vector space is semisimple. Thus the conclusion holds when d=0. Now assume d >= 1. If n > 2d, then X_k is a projective k-scheme of pure dimension d, so lemma_projective_top_degree_vanishing gives H^n_et(X_k,Q_ell)=0, and the zero operator is semisimple. Hence we may assume 0 <= n <= 2d. Since X and Y are smooth projective over F_q, they are proper over F_q. The constant sheaf Q_ell on X_k and on Y_k is lisse, hence constructible, and carries its natural arithmetic Frobenius structure. Applying lemma_45_finite_frob to the constant sheaf on X_k and on Y_k shows that H^n_et(X_k,Q_ell) and H^n_et(Y_k,Q_ell) are finite-dimensional Q_ell-vector spaces. Applying lemma_6a shows that Phi_X and Phi_Y are invertible Q_ell-linear automorphisms. Because f is defined over F_q, the base-changed morphism f_k = f times id_k satisfies f_k o F_Y = F_X o f_k as morphisms Y_k -> X_k: both composites are f times Spec sigma. By functoriality of pullback, this gives f^* o Phi_X = Phi_Y o f^* on H^n_et(X_k,Q_ell). Next apply lemma_77 with m=1 to X and to Y. It gives trace isomorphisms tr_X: H^{2d}_et(X_k,Q_ell) -> Q_ell(-d) and tr_Y: H^{2d}_et(Y_k,Q_ell) -> Q_ell(-d), normalised by closed points, and perfect pairings H^n_et(X_k,Q_ell) x H^{2d-n}_et(X_k,Q_ell) -> Q_ell(-d), (x,y) -> tr_X(x cup y), and H^n_et(Y_k,Q_ell) x H^{2d-n}_et(Y_k,Q_ell) -> Q_ell(-d), (u,v) -> tr_Y(u cup v). For each u in H^n_et(Y_k,Q_ell), the map y -> tr_Y(u cup f^* y) is a Q_ell-linear functional on H^{2d-n}_et(X_k,Q_ell). Since the pairing on X is perfect, the map H^n_et(X_k,Q_ell) -> Hom(H^{2d-n}_et(X_k,Q_ell),Q_ell(-d)) is an isomorphism. Therefore there exists a unique element tau_n(u) in H^n_et(X_k,Q_ell) such that tr_X(tau_n(u) cup y) = tr_Y(u cup f^* y) for every y in H^{2d-n}_et(X_k,Q_ell). This defines a Q_ell-linear map tau_n: H^n_et(Y_k,Q_ell) -> H^n_et(X_k,Q_ell). Let N = deg(f). We prove that tau_n o f^* = N id. For x in H^n_et(X_k,Q_ell) and y in H^{2d-n}_et(X_k,Q_ell), the defining property of tau_n gives tr_X(tau_n(f^*x) cup y) = tr_Y(f^*x cup f^*y). By functoriality of pullback and cup products, f^*x cup f^*y = f^*(x cup y). We now use the top-degree trace compatibility. The morphism f is proper: Y is proper over S=Spec F_q because it is projective, X is separated over S because it is projective, and an S-morphism from a proper S-scheme to a separated S-scheme is proper. Indeed, the graph Gamma_f: Y -> Y times_S X is a closed immersion because X is separated over S, the projection Y times_S X -> X is the base change of the proper morphism Y -> S, and f is the composition of these two proper morphisms. Since f is proper, surjective, generically finite of degree N between smooth projective geometrically connected varieties of pure dimension d over F_q, lemma_top_trace_generically_finite applied to f:Y -> X gives tr_Y o f^* o tr_X^{-1} = N id on Q_ell(-d), hence tr_Y o f^* = N tr_X on H^{2d}_et(X_k,Q_ell). Taking z = x cup y in H^{2d}_et(X_k,Q_ell), we obtain tr_Y(f^*(x cup y)) = N tr_X(x cup y) = tr_X(N x cup y), using Q_ell-linearity of tr_X. Thus tr_X(tau_n(f^*x) cup y) = tr_X(N x cup y) for every y. Perfectness of the pairing on X implies tau_n(f^*x) = N x. Since N is prime to ell, N is a unit in Q_ell. Therefore f^* is injective. Let W = im(f^*) subset H^n_et(Y_k,Q_ell). Then f^*: H^n_et(X_k,Q_ell) -> W is a Q_ell-linear isomorphism. The subspace W is Phi_Y-stable: if w = f^*x, then Phi_Y(w) = Phi_Y(f^*x) = f^*(Phi_X x) by the Frobenius compatibility proved above, so Phi_Y(w) lies in im(f^*) = W. By hypothesis, Phi_Y is semisimple on H^n_et(Y_k,Q_ell). Since H^n_et(Y_k,Q_ell) is finite-dimensional and Phi_Y is invertible, lemma_358 applied to the Phi_Y-stable subspace W gives that the restriction Phi_Y|_W is semisimple on W. Finally, the isomorphism f^*: H^n_et(X_k,Q_ell) -> W intertwines Phi_X and Phi_Y|_W, because f^* o Phi_X = Phi_Y o f^* and the right-hand side lands in W. By lemma_8, Phi_X is semisimple on H^n_et(X_k,Q_ell). Since n was arbitrary, the q-power arithmetic Frobenius is semisimple on H^n_et(X_k,Q_ell) for every n >= 0. This completes the proof.

lemma_product_top_semisimplicity_descent.statement: Let \(q=p^a\) be a prime power, let \(\ell\neq p\) be prime, let \(X\) be a smooth projective geometrically connected variety of pure dimension \(d\ge0\) over \(\mathbb F_q\), and let \(k=\overline{\mathbb F}_q\). If the \(q\)-power arithmetic Frobenius is semisimple on \(H^{2d}_{\mathrm{\acute et}}((X\times_{\mathbb F_q}X)_k,\mathbb Q_\ell)\), then it is semisimple on \(H^n_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(X_k,\mathbb Q_\ell)\) for every integer \(n\ge0\).
lemma_product_top_semisimplicity_descent.proof:
Notation. Write \(H^n:=H^n_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(X_k,\mathbb Q_\ell)\) and \(F_n:=(\mathrm{id}_{X_k}\times\operatorname{Spec}\sigma)^*\), \(\sigma(c)=c^q\), for the \(q\)-power arithmetic Frobenius of \(H^n\). Write \(H^{2d}_{XX}:=H^{2d}_{\mathrm{\acute et}}((X\times_{\mathbb F_q}X)_k,\mathbb Q_\ell)\) and \(\Phi\) for its \(q\)-power arithmetic Frobenius. The hypothesis is that \(\Phi\) is semisimple. By the corpus convention (eoinm/lemma_5), for a finite-dimensional \(\mathbb Q_\ell\)-vector space an operator is semisimple if and only if it is diagonalizable over \(\overline{\mathbb Q}_\ell\); we use "semisimple" and "diagonalizable over \(\overline{\mathbb Q}_\ell\)" interchangeably, and we write \(\overline K:=\overline{\mathbb Q}_\ell\).

Preliminaries (finite dimensionality, invertibility). \(X\) and \(X\times_{\mathbb F_q}X\) are proper over \(\mathbb F_q\). Applying eoinm/lemma_45_finite_frob to the constant sheaf \(\mathbb Q_\ell\) on \(X_k\) (respectively on \((X\times X)_k\)) equipped with its natural arithmetic Frobenius isomorphism \(\psi\), we obtain that every \(H^n\) and every \(H^n_{\mathrm{\acute et}}((X\times X)_k,\mathbb Q_\ell)\) is finite-dimensional over \(\mathbb Q_\ell\). By eoinm/lemma_6a (applied to \(X\) and to \(X\times X\)), each \(F_n\) and \(\Phi\) is a \(\mathbb Q_\ell\)-linear automorphism, with inverse the geometric Frobenius.

Step 1 (a linear algebra claim). Let \(V,W\) be finite-dimensional \(\mathbb Q_\ell\)-vector spaces, \(T\in\mathrm{GL}(V)\), \(S\in\mathrm{GL}(W)\) with \(W\neq 0\). If \(T\otimes S\) is semisimple on \(V\otimes_{\mathbb Q_\ell}W\), then \(T\) is semisimple on \(V\).
Proof of the claim. By eoinm/lemma_5 applied to \(T\otimes S\), the operator \(\overline{T\otimes S}\) is diagonalizable on \((V\otimes W)\otimes_{\mathbb Q_\ell}\overline K\); under the standard \(\overline K\)-linear identification \((V\otimes_{\mathbb Q_\ell}W)\otimes_{\mathbb Q_\ell}\overline K \xrightarrow{\sim} \overline V\otimes_{\overline K}\overline W\), \((v\otimes w)\otimes\lambda\mapsto \lambda(v\otimes w)\) with \(\overline V:=V\otimes_{\mathbb Q_\ell}\overline K\), the operator \(\overline{T\otimes S}\) becomes \(\overline T\otimes\overline S\).
Since \(\dim_{\overline K}\overline W=\dim_{\mathbb Q_\ell}W\ge 1\), the characteristic polynomial of \(\overline S\) is monic of degree \(\ge1\) and splits over the algebraically closed field \(\overline K\); hence \(\overline S\) has an eigenvalue \(\mu\in\overline K\) with a nonzero eigenvector \(w\in\overline W\), \(\overline S w=\mu w\). Moreover \(\mu\neq0\): \(\mu=0\) would mean \(0\) is a root of the characteristic polynomial, i.e. \(\det(\overline S)=0\), contradicting \(S\in\mathrm{GL}(W)\).
Set \(U:=\overline V\otimes_{\overline K}\overline K w\subseteq \overline V\otimes_{\overline K}\overline W\), and put \(A:=\overline T\otimes\overline S\). For \(v\in\overline V\), \(A(v\otimes w)=\overline T v\otimes\overline S w=\mu(\overline T v\otimes w)\in U\); by \(\overline K\)-linearity \(A(U)\subseteq U\). The map \(\iota:\overline V\to U\), \(\iota(v)=v\otimes w\), is \(\overline K\)-linear, injective (pure tensors with the fixed nonzero vector \(w\) are \(\overline K\)-linearly independent whenever the \(v\)'s are), and surjective onto \(U\) by definition of \(U\); and \(\iota(\mu\overline T v)=A(\iota(v))\), i.e. \(\iota\) identifies \(A|_U\) with the operator \(\mu\overline T\). Hence \(A|_U\) and \(\mu\overline T\) have the same minimal polynomial.
Now \(A\) is diagonalizable over \(\overline K\), so its minimal polynomial \(m_A\in\overline K[t]\) is a product of distinct linear factors. Since \(U\) is \(A\)-stable, \(m_A(A|_U)=0\), so the minimal polynomial \(m_{A|_U}\) divides \(m_A\) and is therefore also a product of distinct linear factors. Thus \(m_{\mu\overline T}\) is squarefree. We claim this forces \(m_{\overline T}\) squarefree. Indeed \(\overline T\) is invertible (\(T\in\mathrm{GL}(V)\)), so \(0\) is not an eigenvalue of \(\overline T\) and \(m_{\overline T}(0)\ne0\); writing \(r:=\deg m_{\overline T}\), the monic polynomial \(P_0(t):=\mu^{r}m_{\overline T}(\mu^{-1}t)\) satisfies \(P_0(\mu\overline T)=\mu^r m_{\overline T}(\overline T)=0\), and conversely any monic \(Q\) with \(Q(\mu\overline T)=0\) satisfies \(Q(\mu t)\in(m_{\overline T})\), whence \(Q=P_0\cdot C\) with \(C\) monic, so \(m_{\mu\overline T}=P_0\). The substitution \(t\mapsto\mu^{-1}t\) (\(\mu\ne0\)) is a \(\overline K\)-algebra automorphism of \(\overline K[t]\) preserving coprimality with the derivative, hence \(P_0\) is squarefree if and only if \(m_{\overline T}\) is. Consequently \(m_{\overline T}\) is a product of distinct linear factors over the algebraically closed field \(\overline K\), i.e. \(\overline T\) is diagonalizable over \(\overline K\). By eoinm/lemma_5, \(T\) is semisimple on \(V\). This proves the claim. \(\triangle\)

Step 2 (degrees \(n>2d\)). The base change \(X_k\) is a projective scheme over the algebraically closed field \(k=\overline{\mathbb F}_q\) of Krull dimension \(d\), and \(\ell\neq p=\operatorname{char}k\). By Spark/lemma_projective_cohomology_vanishing (with \(r=d\)), \(H^n=0\) for every \(n>2d\). On the zero space the (unique) operator is diagonalizable, so \(F_n\) is semisimple for all \(n>2d\).

Step 3 (degree \(n=0\)). Since \(X\) is geometrically connected, \(X_k\) is connected; being of finite type over a field it is noetherian with open-and-closed connected components, so its space of connected components is a single point, and the global sections of the constant sheaf are the locally constant \(\mathbb Q_\ell\)-valued functions: \(H^0=\Gamma(X_k,\mathbb Q_\ell)\cong\mathbb Q_\ell\). The map \(F_0\) is induced by the natural arithmetic Frobenius isomorphism \(F_X^{-1}\mathbb Q_\ell\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbb Q_\ell\) of constant sheaves (the \(\psi\) of eoinm/lemma_45_finite_frob); on locally constant functions it is precomposition with the induced self-map of the one-point space \(\pi_0(X_k)\), hence the identity. Thus \(F_0=\mathrm{id}_{\mathbb Q_\ell}\), which is diagonalizable, i.e. semisimple.

Step 4 (degrees \(1\le n\le 2d\)). Fix \(n\) with \(1\le n\le 2d\); then necessarily \(d\ge1\). Put \(m:=2d-n\), so \(0\le m\le 2d-1\) and \(n+m=2d\). If \(H^n=0\) there is nothing to prove, so assume \(H^n\ne0\).

(4a) Non-vanishing of the dual degree. Since \(X\) is smooth projective geometrically connected of pure dimension \(d\ge1\) over \(\mathbb F_q\), eoinm/lemma_77(b) (with \(m=1\), \(Y=X\), \(k=\overline{\mathbb F}_q\)) applies: the pairing \(H^n\times H^{m}\to\mathbb Q_\ell(-d)\), \((x,y)\mapsto\operatorname{tr}(x\cup y)\), is a perfect pairing of \(\mathbb Q_\ell\)-vector spaces. Perfectness means the induced map \(H^n\to\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb Q_\ell}(H^{m},\mathbb Q_\ell(-d))\) is an isomorphism. If \(H^{m}=0\) this target is \(0\), forcing \(H^n=0\), a contradiction. Hence \(H^{m}\ne0\).

(4b) The Künneth summand is Frobenius-stable. Apply eoinm/lemma_81 with both factors equal to \(X\) (which is smooth projective over \(\mathbb F_q\)) and with \(n\) there equal to \(2d\): the Künneth map
\[\kappa:\bigoplus_{i+j=2d} H^i\otimes_{\mathbb Q_\ell}H^j \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ } H^{2d}_{XX}\]
is an isomorphism which carries \(F_i\otimes F_j\) on the \((i,j)\)-summand to \(\Phi\). Let \(S:=\kappa(H^n\otimes H^{m})\subseteq H^{2d}_{XX}\). Since \(F_n\otimes F_m\) preserves \(H^n\otimes H^m\), the identity \(\kappa\circ(F_n\otimes F_m)=\Phi\circ\kappa\) on that summand gives \(\Phi(S)\subseteq S\); and since \(\kappa\) is an isomorphism from a direct sum, its restriction \(\kappa|:H^n\otimes H^{m}\to S\) is a \(\mathbb Q_\ell\)-linear isomorphism with
\[\kappa|\circ(F_n\otimes F_m)=\Phi|_S\circ\kappa|.\]

(4c) Transfer of semisimplicity. By hypothesis \(\Phi\) is semisimple on the finite-dimensional space \(H^{2d}_{XX}\), and \(\Phi\in\mathrm{GL}(H^{2d}_{XX})\) by the Preliminaries. Since \(S\) is a \(\Phi\)-stable \(\mathbb Q_\ell\)-subspace, eoinm/lemma_358 gives that \(\Phi|_S\in\mathrm{GL}(S)\) is semisimple. (Invertibility of \(\Phi|_S\) also follows directly: \(\Phi|_S\) is injective because \(\Phi\) is, and \(S\) is finite-dimensional.) Applying eoinm/lemma_8 to the intertwiner \(\kappa|\) with \(T_V=F_n\otimes F_m\) and \(T_W=\Phi|_S\), we conclude that \(F_n\otimes F_m\) is semisimple on \(H^n\otimes_{\mathbb Q_\ell}H^{m}\).

(4d) Conclusion for this \(n\). We now apply the claim of Step 1 with \(V=H^n\), \(T=F_n\), \(W=H^{m}\), \(S=F_m\). The hypotheses are satisfied: \(V,W\) are finite-dimensional (Preliminaries), \(T\in\mathrm{GL}(V)\) and \(S\in\mathrm{GL}(W)\) by eoinm/lemma_6a, \(W=H^{m}\ne0\) by (4a), and \(T\otimes S=F_n\otimes F_m\) is semisimple by (4c). The claim yields that \(F_n\) is semisimple on \(H^n\).

Conclusion. Steps 2, 3 and 4 cover every integer \(n\ge0\): for \(n>2d\) by vanishing, for \(n=0\) by \(F_0=\mathrm{id}\), and for \(1\le n\le 2d\) by the Künneth-summand argument. Hence the \(q\)-power arithmetic Frobenius is semisimple on \(H^n_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(X_k,\mathbb Q_\ell)\) for every \(n\ge0\), which is the desired conclusion. \(\blacksquare\)

Remark on the suggested route (not used above, and not needed). The embedding \(y\mapsto y\otimes\xi^{d-n}\) proposed in the guidance lands in the \((n,2d-2n)\)-Künneth summand, i.e. in \(H^{2d-n}_{\mathrm{\acute et}}((X\times X)_k,\mathbb Q_\ell)\), not in \(H^{2d}\); it therefore cannot be fed by a hypothesis that only concerns \(H^{2d}((X\times X)_k,\mathbb Q_\ell)\). The argument above replaces it by the full \((n,2d-n)\)-summand, which has total degree \(2d\) by construction, needs no choice of an algebraic class \(\xi\) and no non-vanishing statement for powers of \(\xi\), and needs no hard Lefschetz; the only input besides Künneth is the non-vanishing of \(H^{2d-n}\), supplied by the perfectness of the Frobenius-equivariant Poincaré pairing (eoinm/lemma_77(b)).
